({#jayati#},
 {#jigAya, jigye, ajEzIt-ajezwa, jetum, jita#})
.²1 To conquer, defeat, overcome, vanquish, subjugate; {#jayati tulAmaDirUQo#}
 {#BAsvAnapi jaladapawalAni#} <ls>Pt. 1. 330</ls>; <ls>Bk. 15. 76</ls>, <ls n="Bk.">19. 2</ls>.
.²2 To surpass, excel; {#garjitAnantarAM vfzwiM sOBAgyena jigAya sA#} <ls>Ku. 2. 53</ls>;
 <ls>R. 3. 34</ls>; <ls>Ghaṭ. 22</ls>; <ls>Śi. 1. 19</ls>.
.²3 To win (by conquest, in gambling or in a law-suit), acquire by conquest;
 {#prAgajIyata GfRA tato mahI#} <ls>R. 11. 65</ls>; (where {#ji#} means ‘to conquer’
 also); <ls>Ms. 7. 96</ls>.
.²4 To curb, restrain, control, conquer (as passions).
.²5 To be victorious, be supreme or pre-eminent (generally used in benedictory
 stanzas or salutations); {#jayatu jayatu mahArAjaH#} (in dramas); {#sa#}
 {#jayati pariRadDaH SaktiBiH SaktinATaH#} <ls>Māl. 5. 1</ls>; {#jitamuqupatinA namaH#}
 {#sureByaH#} <ls>Ratn. 1. 5</ls>; <ls>Bh. 2. 24</ls>; <ls>Gīt. 1. 1</ls>.
.²6 To convict.
.²7 To overcome or get the better of (as a disease <ab>&c.</ab>).
.²8 To expect from (with <ab>abl.</ab>).

To cause
 to win or conquer.
